issue.title: Tree-shaking is broken in v8.1.0-beta.0 when using dynamic imports
issue.body: ### Describe the bug Consider an icon library (like https://remixicon.com/) that exposes all of it's icons as individual `export`'s inside an ES6 module script. This icon library is used in a component, like `Icons.vue`, to display icons: ```vue ``` With an `App.vue` like this ```vue ``` You'll get a fair build with proper tree-shaking: ``` vite v8.1.0-beta.0 building client environment for production... ✓ 14 modules transformed. computing gzip size... dist/index.html 0.40 kB │ gzip: 0.28 kB dist/assets/index-BWqhBLA5.js 60.37 kB │ gzip: 23.79 kB ``` Now we'll dynamically import it, for the sake of simplicity using a simple `await import` - in reality this might be an import for a vue-router: ```vue ``` This will result in the whole icon library being bundled: ``` vite v8.1.0-beta.0 building client environment for production... ✓ 15 modules transformed. computing gzip size... dist/index.html 0.40 kB │ gzip: 0.27 kB dist/assets/index-ghH77bth.js 60.36 kB │ gzip: 23.99 kB dist/assets/Icons-B_ZM3gOE.js 2,705.14 kB │ gzip: 515.42 kB ``` Of course the example doesn't make sense in real-life, in reality, as stated before, this would be an import used for a component in a router library for example - that's where I initially faced this bug. ### Reproduction https://github.com/simonwep/reproductions/tree/master/packages/vite-broken-tree-shaking-icon-library ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run `pnpm install` under the package `vite-broken-tree-shaking-icon-library` 2. Run `pnpm build` 3. You should see the whole external library being included, even though only 2 icons are actually imported. ### System Info ```shell System: OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200 CPU: (16) x64 AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor Memory: 33.95 GB / 61.65 GB Binaries: Node: 24.16.0 - C:\Users\Simon\AppData\Roaming\JetBrains\IntelliJIdea2026.1\node\versions\24.16.0\node.EXE npm: 11.13.0 - C:\Users\Simon\AppData\Roaming\JetBrains\IntelliJIdea2026.1\node\versions\24.16.0\npm.CMD pnpm: 10.28.0 - C:\Users\Simon\AppData\Roaming\JetBrains\IntelliJIdea2026.1\node\versions\24.16.0\pnpm.CMD Browsers: Chrome: 149.0.7827.103 Edge: Chromium (126.0.2592.81) Firefox: 151.0.4 - C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe Internet Explorer: 11.0.26100.8115 ``` ### Used Package Manager pnpm ### Logs Log seems to be too long... here's a file instead: [log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29142465/log.txt) ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitejs/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vite.dev/guide). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue. For example, if it's a Vue SFC related bug, it should likely be reported to [vuejs/core](https://github.com/vuejs/core) instead. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A open a [GitHub Discussion](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions) or join our [Discord Chat Server](https://chat.vite.dev/). - [x] The provided reproduction is a [minimal reproducible example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) of the bug.
